question: A building casts a shadow of length 46 m, when the angle of elevation of the sun is 60º .Find the height of the building. (Use sqrt3=1.7)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of building = Shadow length × tan(θ)

h = 46 × tan(60º)

h = 46 × √3

h = 46 × 1.7 = 78.2 m

**∴ The correct answer is 78.2 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the shadow (BC) = 46 m

Angle of elevation of the sun (θ) = 60º

√3 = 1.7

 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
 
 
 60º A B C h = ? 46 m AB = Height BC = Shadow 

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the height of the building be AB = h meters.

⇒ In ΔABC, tan(60º) = AB ÷ BC

⇒ √3 = h ÷ 46

⇒ h = 46 × √3

⇒ h = 46 × 1.7

⇒ h = 78.2 m

**∴ The correct answer is 78.2 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when the object is above the horizontal level.

Key Trigonometric Values

tan(30º) = 1 ÷ √3 | tan(45º) = 1 | tan(60º) = √3

30º-60º-90º Triangle Rule

The sides opposite to the angles 30º, 60º, and 90º are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.
